FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft 
finalized by the Mining Face Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Heavy 
Mechanical Division Council. 

The requirements and dimensions for rock bolts ( resin type ) given in this standard are based 
on practices followed in the industries. Resin capsules have also been covered briefly. Other 
Indian Standards on rock bolts are as follows; 

IS 7578 : 1975 Wedge and slot type roof bolts 
IS 8266 : 1976 Expansion shell type roof bolts 
IS 13219 : 1992 Rock bolts for mines ( cement grouted ) — General requirements 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be 
rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised) 9 . 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded otf value should be the same as that of 
the specified value in this standard. 



IS 13517 :199X 



Indian Standard 
ROCK BOLTS - RESIN TYPE - SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

This standard covers the material and general 
requirements of resin type rock bolts and resin 
capsules for the use in mines and tunnels. 

2 REFERENCES 

The Indian Standards given below are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard: 

IS No. Title 

226 : 1975 Structural steel ( standard 

quality ) ( fifth revision )

( Part 3 ) : 1984 to M 36 ) ( second revision )

and screws ( second revision )

3.1.2 Length of the bolts shall be in between 
1-2 m to 2-4 m. 

3.1.3 Head of bolts may be spiral, splitted or 
threaded type. 

3.1.4 Typical shape of the bolt is given in Fig. 1 

for guidance. 

3.2 Resin Capsules 

3.2.1 The capsules shall be of 26 mm/32 mm/ 
36 mm in diameter (D) and 310 mm in length (L). 

3.2.2 The typical shape of capsule is given in 
Fig. 2 for guidance. 

4 SELECTION CRITERIA 

4.1 The diameter of the bolts shall be selected 
on the basis of rock quality index (R) given 

below: 

Bolt Diameter (d) Rock Quality Index (R) 

20 mm 31 to 50 

22 mm 21 to 30 

24 mm to 20 

4.2 The diameter of the capsules shall be selec- 
ted on basis of hole size given below: 

Capsule Diameter Hole Size 

(P) (*) 

36 mm 43 mm 

32 mm 36 mm 

26 mm 32 mm 

5 TOLERANCES 

5.1 The threads on bolts and nuts shall con- 
form to tolerance class of 8g and 7H respecti- 
vely as given in IS 4218 ( Part 5 ) : 1979. 

6 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 

6.1 Bolts shall be straight, sound and free from 
harmful surface defects. 

6.2 Ends of the bolts shall conform to IS 
1368: 1987. 

6.3 Threads on bolts shall preferably be rolled 
so that the strength of the bolts is not reduced.

7 MATERIAL 



7.1 Berts shall be fabricated from high strength 
deformed steel bar ( ses IS 1786 : 1985 ) or steel 



bar conforming to grade F.410S ( see IS 
226 : r975 ) or steel designation 40C-4 [see IS 
1570 (Part 4) : 1988]. 

7.2 Bearing plates shall be fabricated of F.410S 
( see IS 226 : 1975 ). 

7.3 Nuts shall conform to product Grade — C 
as specified in IS 1363 ( Part 3 ) : 1984. 

8 PERFORMANCE TEST 

The bolts shall be installed properly and then a 
pull of 50 kN shall be applied along the axis of 
bolt. It shall not break/crack and also the 
displacement of bolt shall not be more than 
10 mm. 

9 MARKING 

9.1 Resin bolts shall be marked with the follow- 
ing information at visible place: 

a) Manufacturer's name or trade mark, 

b) Diameter of bolt, and 

c) Length of bolt. 

9.2 Standard Mark 

Details are available with the Bureau of Indian 
Standards. 

10 PACKING 

10.1 Bolts shall be packed in cleaned condition. 

10.2 The capsules shall be packed suitably so 
that they are not damaged during transit. 

11 STORAGE 

11.1 Threads on the bolts shall be kept lubrica- 
ted and suitably protected. 

11.2 Capsules shall not be stored under direct 
sun light and shall not be used beyond 
'Shelf life*. 




LENGTH (L) 



POLYESTER / INNER CASING/

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark 
on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been 
produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system 
of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and 
operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by 
BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under 
which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or 
producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to 

promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality 
certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced 
in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, 
in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type 
or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director 
( Publications ), BIS.
